paras.he: ספר מעגל טוב.
paras.en: The Book Ma'agal Tov

paras.he: אלה בני צעי"ר כל הקורות ודבר גבורות צפו עברו על ראשי ביום לכתי מחנים נפיק לקריתא ארץ העמים ומלכיות שונות ואימות מתחלפות עובר אורחות ימים וכל המרכב שידה תיבה בצבים וכפרדים וצמד גמלים כחדא מחתא. הא גופא קשיא
paras.en: These are the sons of "the young one" (tza'ir) ⚠1: all the happenings and the mighty things that flowed over my head [Lam 3:54] and passed, on the day I went "to Mahanaim" ⚠2, going out to the villages, to the land of the nations, various kingdoms and changing peoples, passing along the paths of the seas [Ps 8:9], and every conveyance, litter and chest, in litters and on mules [Isa 66:20] and a pair of camels, all at one stroke. This itself is difficult.

1.note: A play on "These are the sons of Se'ir" (Gen 36:20): צעיר, "the young one", is the Ḥida's name for himself, and the adventures in the list that follows are his "sons". The closing Aramaic, הא גופא קשיא ("this itself is difficult"), is the formula that opens an objection in the Talmud.

2.he: ביום לכתי מחנים נפיק לקריתא ארץ העמים
2.note: Mahanaim is the place where Jacob met the angels on his way back to the Land (Gen 32:3); Rashi there: two camps, the angels of outside the Land and the angels of the Land of Israel. To "go to Mahanaim" is to cross that border, here on the way out. David also came to Mahanaim (2 Sam 17:24), and David is one of the Ḥida's names. ארץ העמים, "the land of the nations", is the rabbinic term for all lands outside the Land of Israel (b. Shab 15a).

paras.he: אנא זעירא מאנשי ירושלם ת"ו אחזתי ביד ימיני חוטרא לידא ואומר עם קנ"י שיתי שימי שאשית אני סדר אלה מסעי: הערים וחצריהן כמעט שעברתי מהם בקהלות הקדש בשליחות מצוה מעה"ק חברון ת"ו לממני יומי ולממני שבועי: ואתיא מביניא מאשר הפליא חסדו לי בעל הרחמים ית' קצת מן הקצת ועזוזו ונפלאותיו את שיש בהן ידיעה ורשומן ניכר כגון דא צריך לאידועי והיו הדברים להודות ולהלל כל תגמולוהי עלי דלא ליתי לאמנועי: קטונתי מכל החסדים ומכל האמת שגמלני כל טוב כרועה עדרו ירעה. הוא ברחמיו ינחני במעגלי צדק למען שמו והשיב את שבותי חיש ונעופה בתוככי ירושלם עה"ק ת"ו ושם אני מוצא כל שאר בשר חיים וקימים ונזכה ונחיה לעובדו בלב שלם שקטים ושאננים כגנה זרועי: כי"ר.
paras.en: I, the least of the men of Jerusalem, may it be rebuilt, have taken in my right hand a staff for the hand [b. Ket 64a], and I say with my reed pen ⚠2: "shiti", that is, "that I set" [after Rashi on Exod 10:1], the order of these journeys of mine: the cities and their villages, nearly all that I passed through in the holy congregations, on a mission of mitzvah from the holy city of Hebron, may it be rebuilt, by the count of days and the count of weeks ⚠1. And from among them comes a little of the little of the kindness that the Master of mercies, blessed be He, wondrously showed me, and of His might and His wonders: those of which there is knowledge and whose trace is seen. Such a thing needs to be made known, and these words shall be to thank and praise for all His benefits to me, so that I do not hold back. I am unworthy of all the kindnesses and all the truth [Gen 32:11], for He has bestowed every good on me, as a shepherd pastures his flock [Isa 40:11]. May He in His mercy lead me in paths of righteousness for His name's sake [Ps 23:3], and restore my captivity [Deut 30:3]; quickly may we fly [Ps 90:10] into the midst of Jerusalem [Ps 116:19], the holy city, may it be rebuilt; and there may I find all my kin alive and well, and may we merit and live to serve Him with a whole heart, quiet and at ease, like a garden with its sown seed [Isa 61:11]. So may it be His will.

1.he: אלה מסעי ... לממני יומי ולממני שבועי ... במעגלי צדק
1.note: Three phrases give the plan of the book. אלה מסעי recalls the list of Israel's journeys (Num 33:1). "To count days and to count weeks" is the rule for the count of the Omer (Menaḥot 66a): the diary counts its days in the same way. במעגלי צדק (Ps 23:3) gives the first word of the title, Ma'agal Tov.

2.note: Job 29:18, ואומר עם קני אגוע, "I said: I shall die with my nest". The marked קנ"י is read as קנה, the reed pen.

paras.he: שנת תקי"ג.

שבט 4. פ' בא יום ג' נסענו מעה"ק ירושלם ת"ו אני הצעיר עם ח"ש בן חיים זלה"ה למשרת ורבים אשר אתנו לוית חן הם והתפללנו מנחה אצל גד החוזה ואח"ך יצאו נצבים כעשרת בני המן מחלחו"ל. וציערונו והחזירונו כשבויי חרב דרך ארצם ויתר הגז"ם גיזום ואיום והי"ת הפר עצתם ובאנו לשלום לעה"ק חברון ת"ו קרוב לחצות אור לארבעה.
paras.en: 4 Shevat [Tuesday 9 January 1753], the week of Bo, Tuesday: we set out from the holy city of Jerusalem, may it be rebuilt, I the young one, with the sage Samuel ben Ḥayyim, may his memory be for the life of the world to come, as my servant, and many who were with us as a graceful escort. We prayed the afternoon prayer at the tomb of Gad the Seer ⚠2. After that, men of Ḥalḥul came out, standing like the ten sons of Haman, and they harassed us and took us back like captives of the sword by way of their land; and "what the locust left" [Joel 1:4] was threats and menace ⚠1. But the blessed Lord frustrated their plan, and we came in peace to the holy city of Hebron, may it be rebuilt, near midnight on the night of Wednesday.

1.note: יתר הגזם is Joel 1:4, "what the gazam (a locust) left". The marked גז"ם is heard as גיזום, "a threat" (as in גזים, "he threatens", b. Shevu 46a): after they had turned the travellers back, the rest was only threats. The scan has גיזום (the first transcription had ניזום).

2.note: Freimann: Ḥalḥul (חלחו"ל in the next line) is a village between Jerusalem and Hebron, named in Josh 15:58; for the tomb of Gad the Seer he refers to Luncz, Yerushalayim, vol. 1, p. 85.

paras.he: שבט 19. יתרו יום ד' יצאנו מעה"ק חברון ת"ו והעת גשמים ללכת לעזה בחברת שלשה אנשים תלתא דמרחמי.
paras.en: 19 Shevat [Wednesday 24 January 1753], [the week of] Yitro, Wednesday: we left the holy city of Hebron, may it be rebuilt, in the rainy season, to go to Gaza, in the company of three men, three friends.

paras.he: שבט 20. יום ה' לננו אור ה' בכפר הדאוויימ"י בבית שיך נופא"ל ההולך עמנו כי שם ביתו רפת של בקר ויום ה' ציער אותנו הרבה שהיה רוצה שנשבות שם ואגב שוחדא החזיק בדרך.
paras.en: 20 Shevat, Thursday [25 January 1753]: we lodged ⚠1 on the night of Thursday [the evening of Wednesday 24 January] in the village of ed-Dawa'ime, in the house of Sheikh Nawfal, who was going with us, for his house is there: a cattle stall. On Thursday he gave us much trouble, for he wanted us to spend the Sabbath there; and for a bribe he took to the road.

1.note: So printed; read לנו, "we lodged".

paras.he: שבט 21. אור הששי באישון לילה באנו לכפר צומצום ודרך מבוא הכפר שם נקבצו תלי תלים זבל וטיט עמוק ודרך נס יכולנו לעבור במערה מכוערת שערורית עשתה מאד מלאה גלולים ואנשים בה דמות צורות וכל אחד מהם לא אדם הוא כי נח"ש ינח"ש, אינו אלא שרף ועקרב, ואנכי תולעת ואוהבי כצאת השמש באנו לעזה, והאהובים הנז' היו בחברתנו י"ח יום ואותר רק אני וח' שב"ח נ"ע וארכו לנו הימים יותר מחמשים יום ואהוב אחד שבא מעה"ק ירושלם ת"ו נסע דרך יפו שמנה ימים לפני נסיעתנו: ואחר שנסע מצאנו שיך סאלים מהצאלאחייה הן לו הובא ורגליו לנחושתים עם פאש"ה שבא עם הכאזניה מארץ מצרים לשמירת הדרך כי גדול הוא מרישי ברייוני הערביים ונתפשרנו עמו ללכת דרך המדבר דרך סולטאני. וציערת"י בעצמי על שבת זכור שהיינו פורשים מישוב יאודים וברחמיו ית' רצה להתעכב בעזה שבת זכור.
paras.en: 21 Shevat [the evening of Thursday 25 January 1753]: on the night of Friday, in the dead of night, we came to the village of Sumsum. At the entrance of the village heaps upon heaps of dung and deep mud had gathered, and only by a miracle could we pass. [We stayed] in an ugly cave, a very horrible thing [Jer 18:13], full of dung, and the people in it had the likeness of figures; not one of them is a man, for "he surely practises divination" [Gen 44:15] ⚠1; he is nothing but serpent and scorpion [Deut 8:15], and I am a worm [Ps 22:7], and my friends with me. "As the sun goes forth" [Judg 5:31, where the word is "those who love Him"] we came to Gaza. The friends mentioned above were in our company eighteen days, and then only I and the sage Samuel ben Ḥayyim, may he rest in Eden, were left; and the days grew long for us, more than fifty days. One friend who came from the holy city of Jerusalem, may it be rebuilt, traveled by way of Jaffa eight days before we left. After he had gone, we found Sheikh Salim of al-Ṣāliḥiyya ⚠2, "not brought with his feet in fetters" ⚠3: he was with the pasha who came with the treasure caravan ⚠4 from the land of Egypt, to guard the road, for he is great among the chiefs of the Arab brigands [b. Git 56a]. We came to terms with him to go by way of the desert, by the Sultan's road. I was distressed about the Sabbath of Zakhor [17 March 1753], that we would be cut off from any Jewish settlement; but in His mercy, blessed be He, he chose to stay in Gaza over the Sabbath of Zakhor.

1.note: Joseph's words (Gen 44:15), marked so that the reader hears נחש, "snake": they are not men but snakes. The serpent and scorpion of Deut 8:15 follow, and the Ḥida's own "worm" (Ps 22:7) ends the row of creatures.

2.note: Freimann prints the word with vowel points (not shown here). Probably "from al-Ṣāliḥiyya", the town on the desert edge of the eastern Nile delta, on the road to Syria, named after the Ayyubid sultan al-Ṣāliḥ Ayyūb: the sheikh came from Egypt with the pasha. It can also be the name of his tribe or group. Not settled.

3.note: After 2 Sam 3:34, "your feet were not put in fetters". The Ḥida often writes לו for לא (והיא לו נדפס"ה and ל"ו יחרץ at Trento, פשפש ולו מצא near Padua). Read so, the sheikh was no prisoner: he came with the pasha to guard the road, as a chief of the brigands can. The first rendering, "he had been brought in fetters", took לו as "to him"; a prisoner does not fit the man who then leads the caravan. Uncertain.

4.note: Freimann prints the word with vowel points (not shown here); the letter after ז is not clear (ג or נ). Read as khazna, the treasure caravan from Egypt.

paras.he: אדר שני 12. אור מוצאי ש"ק נסענו וביום חנינו במקום הנקרא דיר ובא שיך אחד וציערנו הגם שאו"ל גאפא"ר ושיך סאלים הנז"ל הכהו לפום חורפ"א עד נזיפה ובין חיתא למחבלתא כמה הצער עלה והי"ת ברחמיו לא נתננו טרף לשניהם, ונלוו גוים רבים כשבעים נפשות. ויום הפורים גוים אשר בקרבנו אמרו לכו ונלכה ביום ש"ק והיאודים אגב אונסייהו בלכתם ילכו, ולא נותרה נשמה בי ואני אמרתי לשוא שמרה נפשי ן' יום בעזה צופה ומביט על חלול שבת ונתנפלתי לרגלי שיך סאלים בבכי ותחנונים והי"ת נתנני לחן וחסד ואור לארבעה הלך עמנו וכל השיירה היינו עזובה היינו שכוחה המיר כבודם בלא יועיל ויום רביעי שושן פורים נשיב זיקא רוח גדולה וחזק והלך בסערות והי"ת ברחמיו נתן בנו כח והצילנו.
paras.en: 12 Adar II [the evening of Saturday 17 March 1753]: on the night after the holy Sabbath we set out, and by day we camped at a place called Deir [Deir al-Balaḥ]. A sheikh came and harassed us; he also demanded ghafar [protection money] ⚠4, and Sheikh Salim mentioned above struck him "with the edge of the sword" ⚠5, as far as a rebuke. Between the midwife and the woman in labour ⚠1, how much trouble came up! But the blessed Lord in His mercy did not give us as prey to their teeth [Ps 124:6] ⚠2. Many gentiles joined us, about seventy souls. On the day of Purim the gentiles among us said: come, let us travel on the holy Sabbath day, and the Jews will go when they go, against their will. No breath was left in me [Dan 10:17], and I said: in vain have I guarded [1 Sam 25:21] myself fifty days in Gaza, watching and on guard against desecrating the Sabbath. I threw myself at the feet of Sheikh Salim with weeping and supplication, and the blessed Lord gave me grace and favour; and on the night of Wednesday he went with us. As for the whole caravan, "forsaken" and "forgotten" were the same thing; it exchanged its glory for what does not profit [Jer 2:11] ⚠3. On Wednesday, Shushan Purim [21 March 1753], a wind blew, a great and strong wind [1 Kings 19:11], and it went on in storms; and the blessed Lord in His mercy gave us strength and saved us.

1.note: The proverb of Genesis Rabbah 60:3: "between the midwife and the woman in labour, the poor woman's child is lost". There Jephthah and Phinehas each stand on their dignity, and Jephthah's daughter pays for it; here the travellers suffer while two sheikhs quarrel.

2.note: Ps 124:6, "prey to their teeth" (le-shinnehem); the same letters also read li-shnehem, "to the two of them", the two sheikhs.

3.he: וכל השיירה היינו עזובה היינו שכוחה המיר כבודם בלא יועיל
3.note: היינו עזובה היינו שכוחה is the Talmud's question on Isa 49:14 (Berakhot 32b): "forsaken is the same as forgotten". היינו is "that is", not "we were". The sheikh went on with the Ḥida, and the caravan that had wanted to travel on the Sabbath was left behind; what exactly became of the other travellers is not said.

4.note: הגם שאול is 1 Sam 10:11, "Is Saul also [among the prophets]?". The marked שאו"ל is read as "he asked": he also asked for ghafar. The Ḥida uses the same two words in the same way in the Venice entry. Freimann: the Arabic word is an escort, and more exactly the money paid for protection. He also gives the place: Deir el-Balaḥ (his print has "Balat").

5.note: The biblical "he struck him with the edge of the sword" (לפי חרב) in Aramaic dress, with חרבא, "sword", changed to חורפא, "sharpness", as in the saying לפום חורפא שבשתא (b. BM 96b). עד נזיפה, "as far as a rebuke": nezifah is the lightest kind of ban (b. MK 16a). So the blow was probably one of sharp words. Uncertain.

paras.he: אדר שני 16. ליל ה' באשמורת נאבד ח' שב"ח נ"ע והיה במחשך אישון לילה מצא עצמו כערער בערבה רחוק מהשיירה בבלי דעת אנה יפנה ולא הלך אנה ואנה כי אם צעק יצעק כחצי שעה ולקול צעקתו עירי ושכב"י קול נתנו וישמע את הקול ולו קרב גם את הקול יקח ופורש לעשות לו דרך ובכל זאת אני ישנתי אז והוא כבואו נתעוררתי ולקול הסיפו"ר היתי דואג ושמה.
paras.en: 16 Adar II [the evening of Wednesday 21 March 1753]: on the night of Thursday, in the last watch, the sage Samuel ben Ḥayyim, may he rest in Eden, was lost. It was in the dark of the dead of night; he found himself like a juniper in the desert [Jer 17:6], far from the caravan, without knowing where to turn. He did not go here and there, but only cried out, for about half an hour. At the sound of his cry those awake and those lying down gave voice; he heard the voice and came near to it, and "he took the sound too" [after 2 Sam 19:31], and broke through to make himself a way ⚠1. All this time I was asleep, and when he arrived I woke up, and at the sound of the story ⚠2 I was anxious and appalled.

1.note: After m. San 2:4, of the king: פורץ לעשות לו דרך, "he breaks through to make himself a road". The Ḥida writes ש for צ here, as he writes ארש for ארץ four times in this part. (The first rendering had "a horseman", פרש.)

2.note: The marked הסיפו"ר, "the story", stands where the ear expects השופר: the sound of the shofar at which all the people trembled (Exod 19:16). Uncertain.

paras.he: אדר שני 17. יום הששי בהעלות המנחה קנינו שביתה על פני המדבר קרוב לביר איל עאבד. ויום ש"ק נצטערנו בתוקף השמש בגבורתו. ובעת המנחה נודע בגוים כי רבים לוחמים לפנינו והשיך סאלים אחזתו אחילו. ואנן מה נענ"ה נשברי לב וכהתה כל רוח. ויום א' י"ט בו וליל ב' כל היום וכל הלילה נוסעים אנחנו כי חזק בריח"י. ויום אחד היתה לפני מעבורת כשבולת נהר וארכב על סוס השיך ועברתי וח' שב"ח נ"ע למעלה מגמל כי יעבור במים כרע רבץ הגמל בתוך המים וגם צירה וניצול הכל.
paras.en: 17 Adar II, Friday [23 March 1753]: at the time of the afternoon offering we made our Sabbath rest [cf. Eruvin 51b] in the open desert, near Bir el-Abd. On the holy Sabbath we suffered from the force of the sun in its might [Judg 5:31]. At the time of the afternoon prayer it became known among the gentiles that many fighters were ahead of us, and a fever ⚠3 seized Sheikh Salim. And we, what shall we answer? Broken-hearted, and every spirit faint [Ezek 21:12]. On Sunday, the 19th [25 March 1753], and the night of Monday, all day and all night we traveled, for He has strengthened the bars ⚠1 [Ps 147:13]. One day there was a ford before me like a flowing river; I rode on the sheikh's horse and crossed. The sage Samuel ben Ḥayyim, may he rest in Eden, was up on a camel; as it crossed the water the camel knelt and lay down in the middle of the water, and his provisions ⚠2 too; and everything was saved.

1.note: Ps 147:13, marked as a quotation; apparently a play on בריחה, "flight": the flight was hard. The play returns two entries later: בריחי"ם כלם (Isa 43:14).

2.note: The copy used here shows צירה. The review of this chapter (issue 6) reads צידה in Freimann and in the HebrewBooks copy; the two letters are close in this type. The sense is צידה, "provisions", in both cases. Read again on the scan at high enlargement for this review: resh. The phrase is after וגם צדה לא עשו להם (Exod 12:39).

3.note: Freimann: "the fire of the bones", a fever; the words are from b. Ber 32a (so also b. Git 70a).

paras.he: אדר שני 22. יום ד' עקם הדרך, השיך ראו הביא לנו בתוך כפרי מצרים על נהרותם ועל אגמיהם וכל אילן דמרגג כגן ה' ובדרך הזה בהיותנו אצל שוחה עמוקה השיך הכה הגמל בלי ידיעתי ובתוקף המכה גמלא פרחא ותחתי ארגז ואפול לארץ ומעלה עשן עץ שהיה בידי נשבר והי"ת הטה אלי חסד כי נפלתי קמתי תכף וארכב על הגמל. וכפשע וכו' ח"ו.
paras.en: 22 Adar II, Wednesday [28 March 1753]: he took a roundabout road: the sheikh, "see, he has brought us" [Gen 39:14], into the midst of the villages of Egypt, by their rivers and their pools [Exod 7:19], and every tree pleasant to see [Gen 2:9, Targum Onkelos], like the garden of the Lord [Gen 13:10]. On this road, when we were by a deep pit, the sheikh struck the camel without my knowing it, and from the force of the blow the camel flew ⚠1, and "I trembled in my place" [Hab 3:16], and I fell to the ground; and the wooden pipe ⚠2 that was in my hand broke. The blessed Lord extended kindness to me [Gen 39:21], for "though I fell, I rose" [Mic 7:8] at once and rode on the camel. And but a step, etc. [1 Sam 20:3], God forbid.

1.note: גמלא פרחא, "a flying camel", is the swift camel that the Talmud brings to explain a journey that seems impossible (Makkot 5a); here a blow makes the camel take off. תחתי ארגז is Hab 3:16. Without vowels ארגז is also "a chest", so there is perhaps a second joke: the baggage under the rider.

2.note: מעלה עשן, "smoke-raiser", is the name of the herb that made the smoke of the Temple incense rise straight (b. Ker 6a). Here it is a wooden tobacco pipe.

paras.he: אדר שני 23. יום ה' בערב ראו רכב ופרשים קראו בשמותם כילהי"שאנייטא ובא שליח מאתם והשיך סאלים ירק ירק בפניו ופרחה נשמתו ורכב על הגמל כי בורח הוא. וכל רוח אין בקרבנו בריחי"ם כלם. ונוסף צערי כי הח' שב"ח נ"ע רצה ללכת ברגליו ובמשך שתי שעות ויותר בצער זה אשתהוי אשתהי חצי שעה מטורח פחד ודרך והלילה באנו לכפר א' צוררי הדת.
paras.en: 23 Adar II, Thursday [29 March 1753]: in the evening they saw chariots and horsemen, and they called them by their names: kilhi-shaniyya ⚠1. A messenger came from them, and Sheikh Salim spat in his face [Num 12:14]; and his soul flew from him, and he rode on the camel, for he was fleeing. There was no spirit left in us; we were all fugitives [Isa 43:14]. And my distress grew, for the sage Samuel ben Ḥayyim, may he rest in Eden, wanted to go on foot, and over two hours and more in this distress he lagged behind, he lagged half an hour, from the weariness of fear and road. At night we came to a village of enemies of the faith.

1.note: So printed (in the image perhaps one word); apparently an Arabic or Turkish name for the riders. Not identified.

paras.he: אדר שני 24. יום הו' באנו לכפר מיד גאמיר ושם ד' יאודים ונפרדנו משיך סאלים לשלום ושבתנו שם. ובכפר הנז' יש בה"כ וספרי תורה ומקוה סמוך לבה"כ כי היה קהל גדול לפנים בישראל.
paras.en: 24 Adar II, Friday [30 March 1753]: we came to the village of Mit Ghamr, where there are four Jews. We parted from Sheikh Salim in peace and spent the Sabbath there. In this village there is a synagogue and Torah scrolls, and a ritual bath near the synagogue, for formerly there was a large community there [Ruth 4:7].

paras.he: אדר שני 27. יום ב' נסענו ממיד גאמיר בקאנגי ללכת לבולאק עם גוים רבים.
paras.en: 27 Adar II, Monday [2 April 1753]: we set out from Mit Ghamr in a qanja [a Nile boat] to go to Bulaq, with many gentiles.

paras.he: ניסן 1. יום ה' צער כותש היה בי על השבת נוסף על יגוני שבכל הדרך רבת שבעה לה נפשי אנח"ה עושה וכל דבר קטון למראה עיני באותם הימים כסכנות גדולות וצרות צרורות כי עד הנה לא נסיתי בפרשת דרכים ומדברות ונהרות. וכראות המשרת כי רבים בני שוממה גוים אשר בקרבנו הלכו ביבשה לבולאק רצה ללכת ונתתי לו שני האותות להגביר הר' אברהם מענדיל הי"ו והאיש משתאה וגדלה דאגתי עליו עד שראיתי קא"ק ובתוכו הרב יעקב עמיאל שלוח מהגביר הנז' וקבלני בתוכו.
paras.en: 1 Nisan, Thursday [5 April 1753]: a pounding distress was in me about the Sabbath, added to my grief, for on the whole road my soul was more than sated [Ps 123:4] and sighing; and in those days every small thing seemed in my eyes like great dangers and bound-up troubles, for until then I had not tried crossroads, deserts and rivers. When the servant saw that many of the gentiles among us, "the sons of the desolate" [Isa 54:1], went by land to Bulaq, he wanted to go, and I gave him the two letters ⚠1 [literally "the two signs", Exod 4:9] for the gevir [a wealthy notable of the community] R. Abraham Mendel, may God keep him. And "the man stood wondering" [Gen 24:21] ⚠2, and my worry for him grew great, until I saw a caïque, and in it Rabbi Jacob Amiel, sent by the gevir mentioned above, and he took me into it.

1.note: שני האותות, "the two signs", is Exod 4:9. Read as two letters of introduction to the gevir. Uncertain.

2.note: Gen 24:21: "the man stood wondering at her, keeping silent, to know whether the Lord had made his journey prosper". Probably the Ḥida himself, who waited without news of the servant; less probably the servant.

paras.he: ניסן 2. יום הו' הלכנו למצרים ונתאכסננו אצל החכם השלם השר המ' כמהר"י מנשה יצ"ו והפליא חסדיו עמי. ושם ראיתי ק"ק המצריים ובו צונבאטי וכתוב בק"ק שנבנה בסוף האלף החמשי ומקוה שם וק"ק הרמב"ם ז"ל ובתוכו חדר קטן סגור, אמרו שהיה מושב הרמב"ם ז"ל. ותוך תחום שבת יש עיר אחת וקורין לה מצרים הישנה ושם ס"ת קדוש ונורא, אומרים שהוא ספר עזרא והבה"כ אשר שם, אומרים שבנאו ירמיה הנביא ובתיבה אשר שם היום חרבה התפלל עליה ירמיה, ושם בק"ק ההוא כ"ו עמודי שיש.
paras.en: 2 Nisan, Friday [6 April 1753]: we went to Miṣrayim [Cairo] and lodged with the perfect sage, the minister, the honoured, our teacher R. Y. Manasseh, may his Rock keep him, and he did me wonderful kindnesses. There I saw the synagogue of the Egyptians (Musta'rabim), and in it the Ṣunbāṭī [a Bible codex] ⚠1, and it is written in the synagogue that it was built at the end of the fifth millennium. There is a ritual bath there, and the synagogue of the Rambam, of blessed memory, and inside it a small closed room; they said it was the Rambam's seat. Within the Sabbath limit there is a town they call Old Miṣrayim [Old Cairo], and there is a holy and awesome Torah scroll there; they say it is the scroll of Ezra. And the synagogue that is there, they say that Jeremiah the prophet built it, and on the reader's platform that is there, today in ruins, Jeremiah prayed; and in that synagogue there are 26 marble columns.

1.note: The Bible codex of the synagogue of the Musta'rab (native Egyptian) Jews, which the chronicler Sambari describes. Freimann's note refers to R. Gottheil, JQR 19 (1907), p. 518, who speaks there (n. 2) of "the so-called Sunbāṭi Bible Codex". The Torah scroll that is called Ezra's, later in this entry, is a different book, in Old Cairo.

paras.he: ניסן 30. יום הו' נסעתי עם השר ח"ר רפאל חאייון הי"ו בקאנגי ובאנו לרישיד יום ג' ד' אייר ונתאכסנתי בבית ח' ש"ט אלהאכף הי"ו.
paras.en: 30 Nisan, Friday [4 May 1753]: I set out with the minister, the sage R. Raphael Ḥayyon, may God keep him, in a qanja, and we came to Rosetta (Rashid) on Tuesday, 4 Iyar [8 May 1753], and I lodged in the house of the sage Sh. T. Alhakef ⚠1, may God keep him.

1.note: ש"ט is probably Shem Tov; left as initials.

paras.he: אייר 9. ליל מש"ק נסענו מרישיד וכמו השחר עלה באנו לעיר נא אמון ושם בפתח העיר היו חונים חיל כבד מהפאש"ה ומהבלבול נשתגעו הפרדות להפילנו ונצטערנו הרבה וברחמי שמים נכנסנו לשלום ונתאכסנו אצל החר"י פרובינצאל הי"ו ובאותם הימים שם נמצא הרב החסיד כמהר"א ן' אשר הי"ו והרבו להטיב עמנו. ורחוק מעט מהעיר יש בה"כ נורא מאד ושם כ"ו עמודי שיש וקורין לה ק"ק אליהו שמסורת בידם כי שם נגלה.
paras.en: 9 Iyar [the evening of Saturday 12 May 1753]: on the night after the holy Sabbath we set out from Rosetta, and as dawn rose we came to the city of No-Amon [Alexandria]. There, at the gate of the city, a heavy army of the pasha was encamped, and in the confusion the mules went wild and tried to throw us, and we suffered much. By the mercy of heaven we entered in peace and lodged with the sage R. Isaac Provenzali ⚠1, may God keep him. In those days the pious rabbi, our teacher R. A. [probably Abraham] ben Asher ⚠2, may God keep him, was there, and they did us much good. A little way from the city there is a very awesome synagogue, with 26 marble columns, and they call it the synagogue of Elijah, for they have a tradition that he revealed himself there.

1.note: The print has only the initial י. Freimann's note gives the name without doubt: R. Isaac Provenzali Conorti. Freimann adds that R. Simon von Geldern mentions him, and refers to D. Kaufmann, Aus Heinrich Heines Ahnensaal, pp. 117, 123, 291.

2.note: The print has only the initial א. Freimann: "it seems" that he is R. Abraham ben Asher, who copied the book Sha'arei Kedushah from the writings of R. Ḥayyim Vital. Freimann refers to Benjacob, Otzar ha-Sefarim, p. 604, no. 1136.

paras.he: אייר 26. יום ד' נסענו דרך אניה בלב ים בספינה הסווי"דים ואין די באר מן המצר והני הרפתקי עברו יחדו בלחם ס"ר ויהי הסער לסגור עלי לבי נד ונבדל הולך וחוזר באדוותא דימא גל"י עמיקתא עלו זה שמים לרום אף כי נתעב תוחלת ממושכה {f4} מחלת לענות נפש במספר הימים. ויהי בשלשים יום לנסיעתנו מנא אמון רבה חזה הוית הא להמא עניא אתרחי"ש ליה שם נקבצו משפחת התולע"י אפי' בחדרי חדרים אסו"ר לא יוציאנו גברא דשפיר חזי ואני עני וכואב מחוסר ציד"ה ויר"ק את חניכי"ו לולי ה' שהיה לנו הנמצא כזה אצל בחור יאודי אשר עמנו מעט אורז וממנו נקח בדמים יקרים והינו מגלגלין באורז רק אין דבר פת ופרפרת ויאסרו כל פירות בלתי אל האורז עינינו זה לחמנו ערב ובקר וצהרים בין שפתים ולבי"ן שנים משמש כניסה ויציאה ונפשנו קצה הוה מהדר אסילקא וארוזא ימין מקרבת כי אין בלתו והפה שאס"ר לא תוכל שאתו אמרי לה בחניכת"ו קום ואדיש שלא בטובתו ובשל מבושל במים בגזרי עצים היוצאים מן התיבה אחת היתה בהדי דידי והיתה לשרפה. גם הייתי הלילה אחרת שלא במתכוין משנה מקום משכבי ויהי בחצי הלילה העירני רב החובל ואשא עיני ואראה כל החדר הפוך כמו רגע ובמקום משכבי שם נפלו שידה תיבה ומגדל ויהי לנס. גם רב החובל יחרף צר מסיח לפי טומא"ו על התורה ועל העבודה הוא דאמר הא דדש בעכבי"ו עלי דידן. התהלה והתפארת לחי העולמים כי גבר עלינו חסדו ורוב הימים היינו בנחת וחנינ"ה בסע"ר.
paras.en: 26 Iyar, Wednesday [30 May 1753]: we set out by ship into the heart of the sea, on the ship of the Swedes. There are no words enough to explain the straits [Ps 118:5], and these adventures passed all together, with bread of adversity [Isa 30:20] ⚠1. "The storm was about to close" on me ⚠10; my heart wandered and was cut off ⚠2, going back and forth in the waves of the sea, "the waves of the deep" ⚠11; they mount up to the heavens [Ps 107:26]. And more: hope deferred makes the heart sick [Prov 13:12], to afflict the soul by the number of days. On the thirtieth day of our journey from great No-Amon, I beheld [Dan 7:2] "this is the bread of affliction" ⚠3: what befell it! A family of worms had gathered there, "even in the innermost rooms", a "prisoner" that a man who sees well could not bring out ⚠4. And I was poor and in pain [Ps 69:30], lacking provisions, and "he led forth his trained men" [Gen 14:14] ⚠5. Were it not for the Lord, who was for us [Ps 124:1]: "can we find such a one" [Gen 41:38]? A young Jew who was with us had a little rice, and we bought from him at dear prices, and we got by on rice. Only there was no bread or dessert, and all fruits were forbidden; there was nothing at all except the rice before our eyes [Num 11:6]. That was our bread [Josh 9:12] evening, morning and noon [Ps 55:18], between the lips [Ps 68:14] and "between the teeth" ⚠12, serving entry and exit, and our soul loathed it [Num 21:5]. Someone who used to be particular about beets and rice [Pesaḥim 114b] drew it near with the right hand [b. Sotah 47a], for there was nothing else, and "the mouth that forbade" [m. Ket 2:5] could not bear it [Prov 30:21]. "Some say: by its nickname" [b. Meg 28a]: "Up, and keep quiet" ⚠6, against its will. It was boiled in water [Exod 12:9] with pieces of wood "that came out of the ark" [Gen 9:10], a chest (tevah) that I had with me, and it became fuel [Isa 9:4]. Also, another night, without meaning to, I changed the place of my bed; at midnight the captain woke me, and I lifted my eyes and saw the whole room overturned in a moment, and in the place of my bed a litter, a chest and a cupboard had fallen; and it was a miracle. Also the captain, an enemy, blasphemed [Ps 74:10], talking in his impurity ⚠7 against the Torah and against the worship; he is the one of whom it is said, "one who tramples with his heels" on what is ours ⚠8. The praise and the glory to Him who lives for ever, for His kindness prevailed over us [Ps 117:2], and most of the days we were "at ease, and Ḥanina in the storm" ⚠9.

1.note: Isa 30:20, לחם צר, "bread of adversity", with ס for צ. The marked ס"ר can be heard as the Aramaic סרי, "spoiled, rank", which fits the wormy bread that is told below. Uncertain.

2.note: So printed (ונבדל, not ונבהל); rendered literally.

3.he: רבה חזה הוית הא להמא עניא אתרחי"ש ליה
3.note: Punctuate after מנא אמון רבה, "great No-Amon" (Alexandria). חזה הוית is the "I beheld" of the visions in Daniel 7, followed by the Haggadah's הא לחמא עניא. The "family" of worms plays on the clan of Tola (Num 26:23). אתרחי"ש is "it befell" (as in אתרחיש ניסא, "a miracle happened"); the marked word also holds רחש, "to creep, to swarm".

4.he: אפי' בחדרי חדרים אסו"ר לא יוציאנו גברא דשפיר חזי
4.note: אפילו בחדרי חדרים אסור is the rabbinic rule for a thing that is forbidden even in full privacy (b. Shab 64b). The marked אסו"ר is read as "bound, a prisoner": the worms sit deep inside the loaf, and even a sharp eye cannot get them out. גברא דשפיר חזי, "the man who sees well", is the Targum's wording for Balaam's name for himself (Onkelos on Num 24:3, 15).

5.note: מחוסר צידה is a term of the Sabbath and festival laws for an animal that must still be caught (b. Beitzah 24a); here צידה is "provisions". Then Gen 14:14, וירק את חניכיו. The marked ויר"ק gives ירק, "greens" (he lacked provisions and greens), and also "he emptied"; the marked חניכי"ו is heard as חניכיים, "gums", as in חניכת"ו below: his mouth was empty. Uncertain in detail.

6.note: Freimann gives both sources. ואמרי לה ... בחניכתו, "and some say: [I never called my fellow] by his nickname", are words of b. Meg 27b–28a. In y. Pe'ah 1:1 a son who feeds his father fattened fowl answers the father's question with סבא אכול ואדיש, "old man, eat and be quiet". The marked חניכת"ו is heard as חניכיים, "gums": the palate that had refused rice is told to eat and be silent. (The first rendering, "get up and thresh", was wrong.)

7.note: A twist of מסיח לפי תומו, the legal term for a man who speaks innocently, with no purpose (Yevamot 121b): תומו, "his innocence", becomes טומאו, "his impurity".

8.note: Cf. Avodah Zarah 18a ("commandments that a man tramples with his heels"); the captain mocked the Jewish observances. Uncertain.

9.note: After Ta'anit 24b, where Ḥanina ben Dosa, caught in the rain, says: "all the world is at ease, and Ḥanina is in distress (be-tza'ar)". The Ḥida changes be-tza'ar to be-sa'ar, "in a storm". The marked חנינ"ה can also be heard as "grace": He was gracious to us in the storm.

10.note: Josh 2:5, ויהי השער לסגור, "the gate was about to be shut", with הסער, "the storm", for השער, "the gate".

11.note: Freimann: אדוותא דימא, "the waves of the sea", is from b. BB 4a. גל"י עמיקתא is Dan 2:22, גלא עמיקתא, "He reveals the deep things"; the marked word is read as גלי, "waves of".

12.note: Gen 49:12, ולבן שנים, "and white of teeth", with a yod added: ולבין, "and between".

paras.he: תמוז 23. יום ד' הגענו לנמל ליוורנו.
paras.en: 23 Tammuz, Wednesday [25 July 1753]: we reached the port of Livorno.

paras.he: תמוז 25. יום הו' ירדנו ללאזאריטו בהעלות המנחה ותיכף לסמיכא חדא כרעא אארעא והנה שלשה סלי מלאים כל טוב הארץ מהעוף למינהו וכמה תבשילין וכמה וכמה ככרות וכמה קנקני יינות ופירות לרוב. האחד מהחר"א קאניטי הי"ו והשני מפקידי א"י והג' מהגביר סי' שמואל טדיסקו הי"ו.
paras.en: 25 Tammuz, Friday [27 July 1753]: we went down to the lazaretto [the quarantine station] at the time of the afternoon offering, and at once, as soon as one foot touched the ground, behold, three baskets full of all the good of the land: fowl of every kind, many dishes, many, many loaves, many jugs of wine and fruit in plenty. One was from the sage R. A. Caniti ⚠1, may God keep him, the second from the officials for the Land of Israel [the local agents for its collections], and the third from the gevir Signor Samuel Tedesco, may God keep him.

1.note: The print has only the initial א. Freimann: perhaps R. Abraham Joseph Caniti, author of the responsa Mekitz ben Ḥai (Constantinople 5517, 1757); he refers to Benjacob, Otzar ha-Sefarim, p. 368, no. 2159.

paras.he: אלול ר"ח יום הו' נכנסו לליוורנו יע"א ויתנני ה' לחן וחסד. אך בחלקות סדרן של כתבים נתתי כתב פקידי א"י ואחד מהם כאשר לא ידע לקרותה ארש נתנה ביד אחד חכם ונמצא כתוב דברים קשים נגד הפקידים הישנים על שליחות ההרי"ך הי"ו והם משועי הארץ ואין בהם חטא כלל וכלפי לייא הטו חסדם בענין זה בכל כחם והי"ת נתנני לחן בעיני הגביר הח' המ' איש חסד סי' מיכאל פירירא די ליאון נר"ו והשתדל מאד לכפות פסקתה ולא נודע הדבר. כי ח"ו אלמלא מקרא כתוב ישראל לא ידע היה נזק גדול לשליחות והוקבע הדבר חוב"ה לדור דורים. והג' סי' מיכאל הנז' עם הג' סי שלמה עגיב הי"ו הפליאו לעשות לעזר ולהועיל בענין השליחות. וכפתע פתאום נאספו אנשי המעמד ואהוב אחד שהיתי סומך עליו חש בעינו ולא יכול לבא וצר לי כי הוא מראשי הק"ק. ואחר צאתנו מהמעמד לשלום אמרתי בלבי בקור"ת תהיה להגביר הזה על הודע כי נגמר הדבר לטובה. והנה הוא מתאנה ההוא אמר כי המעמד לא עשו כהוגן לתת סך הרבה כזה והנה ברכתי ברך לצור מנת חלקי הנה נא עצור עצר אותו לחפש"י ישלחנו תחת עינו. ובעיר ליוורנו נשתטחתי על מצבת מהר"ח כהן ז"ל בעל טור ברקת וכו'.
paras.en: 1 Elul, Friday [31 August 1753]: we entered Livorno, may God protect it, and the Lord gave me grace and favour. But "in slippery places", in handing out the letters in their order ⚠7, I gave the letter of the officials of the Land of Israel, and one of them, as he did not know how to read it ⚠1, gave it into the hand of a scholar; and in it were found written harsh words against the old officials about the mission of R. Y. K. ⚠2, may God keep him. They are the nobles of the land and have no fault at all; on the contrary, they had given their kindness in this matter with all their strength. But the blessed Lord gave me grace in the eyes of the gevir, the sage, the honoured, a man of kindness, Signor Michael Pereira de Leon ⚠9, may his lamp shine, and he took great pains to cover up the matter [literally: to turn the bowl over] ⚠3, and it did not become known. For, God forbid, if not for the verse that is written, "Israel does not know" [Isa 1:3] ⚠4, there would have been great damage to the mission, and the matter would have been fixed as a reproach ⚠8 for all generations. The said gevir Signor Michael, with the gevir Signor Solomon Aghib, may God keep him, did wonders to help and benefit in the matter of the mission. Suddenly the members of the council (ma'amad) were gathered. One friend on whom I relied had a pain in his eye and could not come, and I was sorry, for he is one of the heads of the holy congregation. After we came out of the council in peace, I said in my heart: there shall be a visit [Lev 19:20] ⚠5 to this gevir, to tell him that the matter had ended well. But behold, he was seeking a quarrel [2 Kings 5:7]: he said that the council had not done properly to give so large a sum. And then I blessed: blessed be the Rock, my portion; behold, He kept him away: "he shall let him go free on account of his eye" [Exod 21:26] ⚠6. In the city of Livorno I prostrated myself on the tombstone of our teacher R. Ḥayyim ha-Kohen, of blessed memory, the author of Tur Bareket, etc.

1.note: Not a misprint: the Ḥida writes ארש for ארץ three more times in this part (Ancona, Venice, Trento), as he writes ופורש for ופורץ in the desert. The words are perhaps after ויקרא ארץ (Ps 50:1). They add nothing to the plain sense: the man could not read the letter. Uncertain.

2.note: Unresolved initials of an earlier emissary; left as initials.

3.note: After the psakhter, the Temple vessel that was turned over a thing to cover it: over the coals on the Sabbath (m. Tam 5:5), and over a dead creeping thing found in the Temple (m. Eruv 10:15). To turn the bowl over a thing is to hide it. The spelling פסקתה is as printed.

4.he: אלמלא מקרא כתוב ישראל לא ידע
4.note: אלמלא מקרא כתוב, "if the verse were not written", is the Talmud's formula before a bold saying (b. Ber 32a and often). The verse is Isa 1:3, "Israel does not know": things went well only because the community did not come to know of the letter.

5.note: Lev 19:20, marked as a play on בקור, "a visit".

6.note: Exod 21:26, as a pun: the man's eye trouble had kept him from the council, so the matter was settled without him.

7.note: אך בחלקות is Ps 73:18, "surely in slippery places"; the word is also "in handing out" (חלק). סדרן של כתבים echoes סדרן של כתובים, "the order of the Writings" (b. BB 14b).

8.note: חובה is "duty, debt" and also "guilt", the opposite of merit; the word is marked. Rendered "a reproach".

9.note: Freimann: a physician. The Ḥida stayed in his house, and he paid for the printing of the Ḥida's Sha'ar Yosef; the book opens with thanks to him, written by the Ḥida in Spanish. Freimann refers also to the entry of 20 Iyar 5534 [1 May 1774] in the second journey.

paras.he: שנת תקי"ד.
תשרי 25. פ' בראשית יום ה' נסענו מליוורנו וליוונו הרב מהר"ח בונדי והח"ר אליאו הכהן והחר' דוד רקח ה"י ובאנו לפיזה בו ביום וחנינו באושפיזת סופינו.
paras.en: 25 Tishrei, the week of Bereshit, Thursday ⚠1 [the calendar gives Tuesday 23 October 1753]: we set out from Livorno, and the rabbi, our teacher R. Ḥananiah Mazal Tov Bondi ⚠2, the sage R. Eliahu ha-Kohen and the sage R. David Rakaḥ, may God keep them, escorted us; we came to Pisa that same day and lodged at the inn of Supino.

1.note: Printed "Thursday", but 25 Tishrei 5514 was a Tuesday; the next entry has 27 Tishrei as Thursday.

2.note: Freimann: R. Ḥananiah Mazal Tov Bondi wrote the preface to Si'aḥ Yitzḥak on tractate Yoma, the book of his teacher R. Isaac Nunes [Vaez]. The second escort is R. Elijah son of R. Moses ha-Kohen.

paras.he: תשרי 27. יום ה' נסענו והגענו לפלורינציא אור הששי כ"ח בו וחנינו באושפיזת יצחק גאליטי ה"י והלכתי שם בחצ"ר הד"ר ושם ראיתי אריות ונמרים ושאר כנותהן כי חיו"ת הנה ומידי עוברי ראתה עיני גנות הטיול שקורין גיארדינים.
paras.en: 27 Tishrei, Thursday [25 October 1753]: we set out and reached Florence on the night of Friday, the 28th [the evening of Thursday 25 October 1753], and lodged at the inn of Isaac Galletti, may God keep him. There I went into the court of the Duke ⚠1, and there I saw lions, leopards and the rest of their kind, alive, "for they are ḥayot" ⚠2 [Exod 1:19]; and in passing my eyes saw the pleasure gardens they call giardini.

1.note: Both words are marked; read as the court of the grand-ducal palace. Freimann takes the gardens to be the garden beside the palace, and says that the Museo di Storia Naturale close to it has many animals. That museum was founded only in 1775; the live lions of 1753 were kept in the grand-ducal menagerie. The play in the two marked words is not found.

2.note: Exod 1:19: what the midwives say to Pharaoh about the Hebrew women. The word ḥayot is read there as "lively", as "midwives" (Rashi, after the Aramaic ḥayta) and as "beasts" (Sotah 11b). Here it is marked as a pun, and it can mean either that he saw the animals alive, in the Duke's menagerie, or simply that they are wild beasts. Cf. "as if, God forbid, a wild beast (ḥayah ra'ah) had come" a few entries later.

paras.he: חשון 3. פ' נח יום ד' נסענו מפלורינציא והגענו לסיינה יום ה' ד' בו ונתאכסנתי אצל סי' משה דוד גאליקו נ"ע והעיר גדולה ואנשים בה מעט מבני ישראל יראי ה' ותפלתם בנחת ובנעימה קדושה.
paras.en: 3 Ḥeshvan, the week of Noaḥ, Wednesday [31 October 1753]: we set out from Florence and reached Siena on Thursday, the 4th [1 November 1753], and I lodged with Signor Moses David Gallico, may he rest in Eden. The city is large, and the Jews in it are few [Eccl 9:14], God-fearing, and their prayer is calm and in holy sweetness.

paras.he: חשון 7. לך לך יום א' נסענו מסיינה דרך הרים וגבעות והגענו לעיר מונטי סאן סאבינו יום ב' בערב ח' בו. ובפתח העיר הללו בעלי פטישי"ן חרשי ברזל ופעל בפחם כראותם אותנו רוח עועים לבשה אותם והתחילו מכים בפטיש על הסדן וצועקים כאלו ח"ו חיה רעה באה וקול הקריה הומה נאספו אנשים והטף צועקים ושוחקים והנה אנחנו באים בארץ בושים ונכלמים יראים ונבהלים ואנחנו לא נדע על מה זה ואנה נפנה והגוי ההולך עמנו לא ידע דרך מחוז היאודים ורבו מצערו"ת ראשנו עד כי נער ישראל הן הראנו באיזה דרך נלכה נא לבתי היאודים וכשהגענו ליאודים אין מאסף אותנו. והשעה דחוקה לתפלת המנחה אז אמרתי בית ה' נלך ותעבור המנח"ה וערבית ויפקד מקום ללון וכצאתנו מבה"כ ירד ירדנו בתחלה לבית אחד סמוך ריקם ריקם והחלונות פתוחות והזמן קר בימות החורף ובאו עמנו איזה אנשים אז אמרתי מי הוא הפרנס כאן ענה אחד מהם אני אני הוא, אמרתי לו אוי לו לדור שאתה פרנסו, הטוב בעיניך לזלזל בשליח א"י כאחד הפחתי"ם רק אין יראת אלדים במקום הזה וכל כי הני מילי בתוכחות על עון ודברי בנחת נשמעים ונכנסו הדברים כארס של עכנא הוא יקראנ"י לסור אל ביתו ואל חדר הורתו ואני סרבתי קצת וסוף דבר עמו אנכי הלכנו לביתו. וקריתי שם ספר תומר דבורה להרמ"ק ז"ל.
paras.en: 7 Ḥeshvan, [the week of] Lekh Lekha, Sunday [4 November 1753]: we set out from Siena by way of mountains and hills and reached the town of Monte San Savino on Monday evening, the 8th [5 November 1753]. At the gate of the town these hammer-men, smiths of iron who work in the coals [Isa 44:12], when they saw us, a spirit of confusion [Isa 19:14] took hold of them, and they began to beat with the hammer on the anvil and to shout, as if, God forbid, a wild beast had come; and the noise of the town was in an uproar [1 Kings 1:41]; men gathered, and the children shouting and laughing. And here we were, coming into the land ashamed and humiliated, afraid and confused, not knowing why, nor where to turn. The gentile who went with us did not know the way to the Jews' quarter, and our sorrows were "more than the hairs of our head" ⚠1, until a Jewish lad [Hos 11:1] showed us which way we should go to the houses of the Jews. When we reached the Jews, no one took us in [Judg 19:15]. The time for the afternoon prayer was short; then I said: let us go to the house of the Lord [Ps 122:1]. "The minḥah passed" [Gen 32:22], and the evening prayer, and "the place was empty" [1 Sam 20:25] ⚠2: there was nowhere to sleep. When we came out of the synagogue we went down first to a house nearby, quite empty, with the windows open, and the season cold, in the days of winter. Some men came with us. Then I said: who is the warden here? One of them answered: I, I am he. I said to him: woe to the generation whose warden you are [b. Ber 28a]! Does it seem good in your eyes to slight an emissary of the Land of Israel like one of the lowliest [a play on 2 Sam 17:9, "in one of the pits"]? Surely there is no fear of God in this place [Gen 20:11]; and more such words of rebuke about the sin. And words spoken calmly are heard [Eccl 9:17]: the words went in like the venom of a snake. He invited me to turn aside to his house, to the chamber of her who conceived him [Song 3:4]; I refused a little, and in the end, "I am with him" [Ps 91:15], we went to his house. There I read the book Tomer Devorah by Moses Cordovero, of blessed memory.

1.note: Ps 69:5, רבו משערות ראשי, "more than the hairs of my head", with מצערות, "than the sorrows of", for משערות.

2.note: Two verses. Gen 32:22, ותעבר המנחה, "the gift passed over", with minḥah as the afternoon prayer. Then 1 Sam 20:25, ויפקד מקום דוד, "David's place was empty": David is one of the Ḥida's names, and he had no place for the night.

paras.he: חשון 11. יום ה' נסענו דרך הרים הגבוהים וכמעט כל הדרך הרים סביב ודרך מסוכן ובאנו לליפייאנו אור הו' י"ב בו ושם ה' או ו' בעלי בתים ונתאכסנתי אצל הזקן ה"ר אליה די לה אקווילה ושם מצאתי ספר תורת חכם למהר"ח הכהן ז"ל ונשתעשעתי בו.
paras.en: 11 Ḥeshvan, Thursday [8 November 1753]: we set out by way of high mountains, and nearly the whole way there were mountains all round and a dangerous road, and we came to Lippiano on the night of Friday, the 12th [the evening of Thursday 8 November 1753]. There are five or six householders there, and I lodged with the elder R. Elijah dell'Aquila. There I found the book Torat Ḥakham by our teacher R. Ḥayyim ha-Kohen ⚠1, of blessed memory, and I took delight in it.

1.note: Freimann: sermons on the order of the Torah by R. Ḥayyim son of R. Abraham ha-Kohen of Aleppo, printed in Venice in 5414 (1654); he also wrote Mekor Ḥayyim on the Shulḥan Arukh. He is the author of Tur Bareket, at whose grave the Ḥida prayed in Livorno.

paras.he: חשון 15. פ' וירא יום ב' נסענו מליפייאנו והגענו לעיר אורבינו אור לארבעה טו"ב חשון הזאת העיר ראשית ממלכת האפיפיור ובני ישראל אשר שם עניים מרודים.
paras.en: 15 Ḥeshvan, the week of Vayera, Monday [12 November 1753]: we set out from Lippiano and reached the city of Urbino on the night of Wednesday, the seventeenth ⚠1 of Ḥeshvan [the evening of Tuesday 13 November 1753]. This city is the first of the Pope's dominion, and the Jews who are there are wretchedly poor.

1.note: טו"ב is 17 (9 + 6 + 2), written so as to spell "good". The night of Wednesday 17 Ḥeshvan 5514 was the evening of Tuesday 13 November 1753, so the date and the weekday agree.

report: Pages 1-5 done: the book title, the Ḥida's two opening paragraphs, the year headings 5513 and 5514, and the entries from 4 Shevat 5513 to 15 Ḥeshvan 5514 (Jerusalem, Gaza, Egypt, Livorno, Tuscany, Urbino). OCR fixes were mostly ג read as נ (כגון, גדולות, גבוהים, גבעות, מיד גאמיר, קאנגי), plus ס/פ (הפרדות, הפחתים), ס/ב (בק"ק, בסוף), ו/י (וסוף) and footnote numbers stuck to words; the handwritten pencil '(1753)' beside the first year heading is not printed text and is left out. Please check: the title paragraph has start '1:0' because input.txt does not hold the title line; 25 Tishrei 5514 is printed 'Thursday' but was a Tuesday; and the dense wordplay of the sea-voyage paragraph (3:31) has eight uncertain renderings.
